records.name: Kadampa Meditation Center Philadelphia
records.summary: A Buddhist meditation center on North 2nd Street with weekly classes on Sunday, Monday, Wednesday and Thursday, plus a monthly Prayers for World Peace session on the first Friday.
records.what_you_do: Take a weekly meditation class, come to the free monthly Prayers for World Peace, or join a series such as Meditation 101. Most classes cost $15 and the Thursday morning class costs $5, and a $50 monthly membership covers the general classes.

schedule.text: Sunday morning meditation 10:30 to 11:45 am. Monday Rest and Reflect 7 to 8 pm. The Power to Change on Wednesdays 7 to 8 pm. Thursday morning meditation 8 to 8:30 am. Prayers for World Peace on the first Friday of the month, 7 to 8 pm.

cost.text: Most classes cost $15 and the Thursday morning class costs $5. A monthly membership of $50 covers the general classes. Prayers for World Peace is free.

first_step.how: Pick a class on the classes page and register online, or call 267-702-3817 (voicemail; they call back). The FAQ says you can also drop in if you arrive 10 to 15 minutes early to sign in and pay.
first_step.basis: Each class says beginners are welcome with no experience needed, and the FAQ says classes suit beginners and experienced meditators. Rated 4 rather than 5 because the class listings say registration is required and the beginner series is not stated as repeating.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each class opens with a short introduction, then a guided breathing meditation and a short teaching on Buddhist thought, and ends with a closing meditation. Sunday mornings run 10:30 to 11:45 am and the evening classes run an hour, 7 to 8 pm. You can stay afterward to ask the teacher questions or browse the bookstore.
first_visit_tips: Arrive 10 to 15 minutes early: doors lock 5 minutes after the start, and late arrivals cannot be seated.
The entrance is on Cuthbert St. Take your shoes off in the hallway before the meditation room, where benches are provided.
Nothing special is needed to bring or wear. A pen and notepad are handy if you take notes.
Food and drink stay in the lounge, not the meditation room.

records.notes: Class dates on the classes page have no year, and the only year on the site is a 2022 footer, so no last_sign_of_life was set. The Power to Change and Thursday morning classes are marked new with September start dates but no year, so they were not used as dated evidence. Class listings say registration is required while the FAQ says drop-in is possible; confirm when booking. Ardmore (PA) and Collingswood (NJ) branch classes are outside Philadelphia and left out of this record. The membership page's admin email is for membership questions, so it is not recorded as a general contact. Accessibility (wheelchair, elevator) and parking are not on the pages read.

records.name: Kensington Corridor Trust
records.summary: A nonprofit trust that acquires and develops affordable homes and shops along Kensington Avenue, so that local residents and business owners keep a say over how the property is used. It shares news updates and a business directory.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for news, browse the Business Directory or the For Renters page, read about Community Ownership, or donate. To ask how to take part, email the trust.

cost.text: No event costs are listed. The site links a donation page and a merchandise store.

first_step.how: Email info@kctphilly.org to ask how to take part, or sign up for news on kctphilly.org. The newsletter form showed a setup note when checked, so email may be the surer route.
first_step.basis: The site lists news, a business directory and ways to donate, but describes no volunteer role, membership or public meeting, so the way into hands-on involvement is unclear.

records.notes: The site lists no events, meetings or office hours, so no first-visit description was written. The copyright footer reads 2026 but has no month, and footers are not evidence, so no last_sign_of_life was set. The support page lists donating a property, mission-aligned investment (ask the trust), a check payable to the trust, an online donation page, and a merchandise store. The earlier record said renters and investors pages; corrected to the For Renters and Community Ownership pages. The contact name Casey Odonnell comes from the IRS and NCCS data and does not appear on the pages read. Social accounts are Facebook, Instagram and a Twitter handle (@KCTPhilly); no URLs were confirmed, so none are recorded.

records.name: Kingdom and Community Connections
records.summary: A faith-based service ministry that offers counseling, mentoring, job skills training, money training, and parenting workshops. The ministry says it serves people who may or may not attend church.
records.what_you_do: Join a program such as the men's coaching group, the mentoring program for young women, financial freedom training, or employment skills help. The group also runs a meal assistance program and makes referrals to other agencies.

cost.text: Program fees are not listed on the site.

first_step.how: Call 215-232-3900 or email info@kcconnections.org and ask which program fits you. The site does not list start dates or an intake step.
first_step.basis: Each program is described, but the site gives no start dates, intake steps or sign-up process and asks visitors to call or email to ask, so the way in is unclear.
first_visit_tips: Call or email before you come, since program times and fees are not listed.
Ask whether the program you want is open to people who do not attend church; the ministry says it serves people who may or may not attend.

records.notes: The program, contact and services pages (/programs, /contact-us, /services) returned 404, so the homepage was the only source of program detail. No start dates, times or fees appear on any page read, so no schedule was written and the first visit is not described. The site calls itself a Christian ministry but names no denomination, so audience.faith is left out. Added food_pantry for the meal assistance program (Bread of Life Ministry). The contact name is from the IRS and NCCS data and does not appear on the pages read.

records.name: Kol Tzedek
records.summary: A Reconstructionist synagogue in West Philadelphia. Members pray on Shabbat, study in the Torah school and adult classes, and can join a virtual community.
records.what_you_do: Come to Friday evening or Saturday morning services, enroll children in the Torah school, take an adult learning class, or become a member. A newsletter sign-up is on the site.

schedule.text: Friday evening service at 6:30 pm, hybrid or online. Saturday morning service at 10 am in person, followed by a lunch. Torah School meets Sunday afternoons, 3:15 to 5:30 pm, for kindergarten to 7th grade.

cost.text: Membership runs on a sustaining share. The page prints the 5785 figures as $180 a month or $2,160 a year, with a suggested minimum of $36 a month, and says money should not be a barrier to membership. No price for visiting services or for Torah School tuition is printed.

access.notes: Accessible front door with a push button into the lobby, an ADA restroom, and a handicapped parking spot directly in front of the sanctuary on Whitby Ave. The page does not mention an elevator or ramp. Friday services are live-captioned, and ASL is available for High Holiday services when requested at least 30 days ahead. Fidgets and headphones can be borrowed during services.

first_step.how: Come to the Friday 6:30 pm service, hybrid or online, or the Saturday 10 am service in person. For Torah School, use the Register Now form on the Torah School page, or call the Torah School Director at 267-629-2349.
first_step.basis: The Shabbat page welcomes first-time guests, and the membership page gives a form and a staff contact to start; no guest orientation is described, so it is a 4 rather than a 5.
first_step.what_to_expect: Friday services run about an hour and a half, and Saturday services run two to two and a half hours, mostly in Hebrew. The page welcomes first-time guests and has no dress code, but it does not say where to check in or whether there is a sign-in step. The cost of attending as a guest is not printed.
first_visit_tips: Street parking on Whitby Ave is not guaranteed. A handicapped spot is directly in front of the sanctuary, and the Director of Operations can hold nearby parking if you ask ahead.
Fidgets and headphones can be borrowed during services; they sit next to the prayerbooks.
The prayerbooks are Siddur Chaverim Kol Yisrael on Friday and P'tach Libi on Saturday. The page does not say whether copies are provided.

records.notes: The Shabbat page's Friday services change starting September 2026, which is the newest dated evidence and sets last_sign_of_life. Other dates on that page (summer Friday services in July and August, Shabbat Zimra dates listed as 5787) are not written with a year, so they were not used. The Torah School page gives a 2026 to 2027 school year, and non-members may attend for one year before joining. Tree House: KT After School (grades K to 6, Wednesdays 3:30 to 6 pm, from August 26, 2026) and Hebrew Hevruta are related programs, not written into the schedule. Not read because the fetch budget ran out: the Getting to KT page (no nearest SEPTA stop recorded), the Hineini conversion cohort (a possible newcomer program that could support a 5 rating), and the Adult Learning page. Dues figures are labelled 5785 on the page and may be out of date. The Director of Operations and Torah School Director names are not recorded.

records.name: Korean Community Development Services Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit in the Olney area that helps new immigrants and low-income families with housing, naturalization help and benefit enrollment, and runs an early learning center.
records.what_you_do: Call 202-821-8591 to ask about housing, immigration or benefits help, or about the early learning center. Housing, benefits and immigration help is by appointment.

schedule.text: Housing, benefits and immigration services are by appointment, weekdays 9 am to 5 pm. The early learning center is open weekdays 7 am to 6 pm.

cost.text: The site does not list fees for housing, benefits, immigration help, or the early learning center.

first_step.how: Call 202-821-8591 to book an appointment for housing, benefits or immigration help, or to ask about the early learning center. The site also has a contact page.
first_step.basis: The site says it serves new immigrants and gives a phone number to start, but housing and childcare are for low-income families and the eligibility rules are not described.
first_step.what_to_expect: Housing, benefits and immigration help is by appointment, and staff guide you through each application, including naturalization and benefit sign-ups. The page does not say how long a visit takes, what papers to bring, or what it costs.
first_visit_tips: Book by phone first: housing, benefits and immigration services are by appointment only.
The office is at 6055 N. 5th St. The early learning center is at a different address, 5224 Rising Sun Avenue.
Ask about languages and eligibility when you call, since the site does not list either.

records.notes: The homepage shows only a 2024 copyright footer, which is not evidence, and no dated news. Its case study section contains placeholder text, so nothing from it was used. Office hours conflict: the group's own page gives 9 am to 5 pm weekdays by appointment, while a separate listing gives 8 to 5 (not used). The immigrant support page linked from the site was not in the fetched content. Eligibility for housing and early learning (low-income families) is not described in detail. The group's name suggests a Korean community focus, but the pages read do not say so, so no heritage tag was added. Staff languages and walk-in policy for childcare are not stated.

records.name: La Guagua 47 Community Arts Project
records.summary: A multi-year arts residency at Taller Puertorriqueño that helps neighbors shape La Guagua 47, a bilingual Puerto Rican musical about migration and belonging in Philadelphia. Workshops in storytelling, music, dance and visual art invite neighbors, youth, elders and families, and the group also presents concerts and street performances.
records.what_you_do: Join a workshop in storytelling, music, dance, visual art or cultural memory, help make parade floats or decorations, or come to a concert or street performance. The workshops are open spaces where community members shape the show, not auditions.

schedule.text: Workshops and performances are one-off events, announced as they are scheduled.

locations.label: Parks, schools and festivals in Philadelphia

cost.text: Free community programs and workshops, per the project page. The September 2026 concert is listed with free admission, backed by sponsors. Check other performances for any ticket price.

first_step.how: Call Taller Puertorriqueño at 215-426-3311 or email info@tallerpr.org to ask about the next workshop or free performance. The project's own site does not list dates.
first_step.basis: The residency page invites neighbors to join workshops, but it gives no workshop dates, sign-up or RSVP steps, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: Residency workshops are open spaces where you help shape the show through storytelling, music, dance, visual art or cultural memory. The page says they are not auditions or performances, and it gives no times, length or sign-up steps. Past community events included a parade float workshop and an intergenerational flower-making workshop, but the cost of a workshop is not stated.
first_visit_tips: Confirm the date, time and place with Taller before you go, since the project pages list none.
The residency is based at Taller Puertorriqueño, 2600 N 5th St.
The musical is bilingual with some Spanish throughout; the language used in workshops is not stated.

records.notes: The project's homepage contains only a title line, and its /about page returned 404, so most detail comes from the Taller Puertorriqueño residency page and a ticket listing. The Taller page lists 2025 events (a parade float workshop, an orchestra premiere, Story Fest, a flower workshop) without months, and 2026 plans (a June 2026 concert presentation, a July 2026 street performance) with no sign-up step. The September 26, 2026 concert at Taller (7 to 8 pm, free admission per the listing's sponsors) is the newest dated item and sets last_sign_of_life; the listing's button reads join the wait list, so it may have been full. The project contact email on the Taller page is a personal address, so it is not recorded. The 2026 and 2025 events are dated, so they are kept out of schedule.text. The search summary said the current date was October 9; the batch date of 2026-10-08 was used. Search budget: 1 WebSearch used.

records.name: La Liga del Barrio
records.summary: A basketball league for boys and girls ages 6 to 18, with an adult division for players 19 and up. It runs a winter league and a summer season, and each player receives a jersey.
records.what_you_do: Players register for a season, are placed on teams through a draft, and join scheduled league games, including Saturday games in the winter league. Volunteers can coach, help plan events, or do outreach.

schedule.text: Winter league: scrimmages in early December, a draft in early January, and nine Saturday games in January. The league also runs a summer season. Game and practice times are not stated.

cost.text: The site says fees are among the lowest in the city, but it gives no amount.

first_step.how: Register online through the sign-up link for your division: boys or girls 6 to 11, girls 12 to 18, boys 12 to 18, or adults 19 and up. Sign up early, because spots fill quickly.
first_step.basis: Registration is public and clear, and the league offers Spanish-language support, but the site does not describe tryouts or skill levels, and players are placed through a draft.
first_step.what_to_expect: Sign-up comes first. Players are placed on teams through a draft held in early January for the winter league, and the winter season has early December scrimmages before nine Saturday games in January. Each player receives a jersey, and the site does not list game or practice times.
first_visit_tips: Register early, since spots fill quickly and the site gives no deadline.
Ask the league for game and practice times and the home court, since the site does not list them.

records.notes: The site's own pages show 2026 registration for the summer season (June 27 to August 15, 2026), which sets last_sign_of_life to 2026-06. Game and practice times and regular venues are not on the site; the only venue named is Community College of Philadelphia for championship games (April 2025). The site describes the adult division as an alumni league for ages 19 to 35, started in 2021. The community tag latino comes from the site's description of the league as for Latino youth and other young people in the city; open_to stays public. The season field is left out because the league runs a winter league and a summer season. The site has no phone or email, only a contact form. The 2025 Liga Gala date (tentatively October 4, 2025) is past. Pages /register/, /faq/ and /who-we-are/ returned 404 (guessed URLs).
